correctness.rationale: Proof derives the exact invariant-coordinate Lindblad evolution (with missing orbit conventions at a=1,b=1), proves strict relaxation by the negative Hilbert–Schmidt off-diagonal form and graph connectivity, integrates its initial-to-stationary equations and solves for the return integral. The coefficient K>0 and R>0 for n>=3, with R=0 only at n=2, giving a unique strict minimum and both asymptotic regimes. Independent full-complex-matrix finite numerical resolvents and exact-rational orbit identities are replayed from the packaged verifier; those finite tests corroborate but do not establish the all-size claim.

value.rationale: This is an exact nontrivial zero-frequency quantum-return diagnostic for an analytically natural but structurally asymmetric family, providing a unique optimal noise strength and two sharply distinct size-scaling regimes (fixed initial part versus proportionate parts). The result quantifies noise-assisted decay versus Zeno localization, and the difference between initial vertex centralities, not merely re-labelling a known table or offering a tiny numerical gain. The derived optimal gamma scales as J sqrt(b) or Jn depending on graph geometry, relevant to selection of dephasing strengths in finite coherent transport. More specifically, the measured return functional is the time-integrated connected equilibrium occupation autocorrelation normalized by its initial variance, with reference state I/n; thus it is a natural zero-frequency quantity, not an arbitrarily chosen oscillatory area.
